jobs.title: MIT- Software Engineer Intern | Engine
jobs.description_text: Position Overview As a Software Engineer, Intern, you'll have the opportunity to spend 12 weeks working on one (or more) of the engineering teams at SingleStore. You will be at the forefront of real-time technology that’s revolutionizing how companies run their businesses every day. With a continuous release cycle, our engineers are accustomed to moving quickly in a rapid production environment. To do this successfully, we work collaboratively and creatively across teams to maximize our opportunity for impact. We also believe it’s important to celebrate our wins together, whether it be at a local spot or getting out of the city for some exploring. As a Software Engineer, Intern, you will be empowered to own your projects end-to-end and be an active contributor throughout the product life cycle. To expedite your growth path, you will partner with engineers who deeply care about your success and will lend their expertise to your professional development. Our engineers are not just technical partners/mentors, but are also business partners who are exposed to all areas of the business, working with teams such as product, marketing, and sales. Our interns are responsible for projects that are deployed continuously into production over the course of their internship. Your work will include everything from writing new features to testing software and you’ll gain a significant understanding of both the product and the business. Required Skills and Experience Enrolled in a B.S. Degree

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer
jobs.description_text: About SingleStore SingleStore delivers a real-time, distributed SQL database that unifies transactional and analytical workloads. Our engineers build cloud-native software for some of the world’s most demanding data-intensive applications, working in a fast-moving environment where teams own their work end to end and partner closely across Product and customer-facing organizations. About the Flow team SingleStore Flow is an enterprise data migration and integration product that helps customers move data into SingleStore reliably and at scale. The team builds the systems that support schema transfer, bulk data loading, real-time Change Data Capture (CDC), large-table migrations, and a native experience in SingleStore Helios. Flow spans Java-based engines, source and destination connectors, database internals, performance and memory management, Helios services and APIs, observability, test automation, Flow AI Agent and signed production release delivery. The product works across heterogeneous database environments, including MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, MongoDB, SAP HANA, Snowflake, Salesforce, and SingleStore-as-a-source. Position Overview We are looking for a Staff Engineer to provide technical leadership for Flow’s end-to-end data path from source systems and CDC through migration engines, APIs, Helios, and the customer experience. jobs.title: Support Engineer
jobs.description_text: Position Overview Our customers are at the forefront of some of the most interesting data in the world, using SingleStore to push the boundaries every day. This Support Engineering role skews far more towards engineering than typical technical support as you will need to delve into database internals and memory allocators, investigate Linux and host-related configurations, and diagnose SQL query behavior, all in the name of resolving complex database issues. Our Support Engineers are constantly learning a wide range of customer systems and technical concepts and are thrilled by the new and exciting challenges that they encounter on a regular basis. jobs.title: Director, Finance AI & Automation
jobs.description_text: The Finance organization at SharkNinja is a strategic partner that enables innovation, accelerates growth, and drives outstanding business performance. Working closely with Finance partners to support Product Development, Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, and Commercial teams, providing the insights and financial leadership that enable SharkNinja to deliver disruptive, consumer first innovation. As the Director, Finance AI & Automation , you will own the design, build and deployment of the AI capability inside a global Finance organization at a nearly $8 billion consumer products company. This is not an advisory or program management role. You will personally build, production AI agents and automations that change how Finance plans, closes, controls, and decides. You will be deployed across the whole Finance estate, FP&A, Accounting, Internal Audit and SOX, Tax, and Treasury. SharkNinja measures this work in gross margin dollars, headcount productivity, and enterprise value. It is not measured in hours saved. As Finance moves from a handful of agents to an estate of them, you will build and run the agent register, the control tiering that goes with it, and the standards that keep an automated process auditable in a SOX environment. jobs.description_text: The Director of Embedded Firmware is a senior US-based firmware leader, accountable for both the technical direction and architecture that governs firmware across SharkNinja's global portfolio, and the delivery of firmware for SharkNinja products. On the delivery side, this leader is responsible for overseeing the US firmware development organization including managing both internally and externally generated embedded firmware across the complete SharkNinja product portfolio. This role is a peer to the Connected Firmware director, who owns connected embedded architecture and delivery, and coordinates with the Embedded Firmware director in Asia on embedded firmware delivered in that region. Key Responsibilities Architecture & Technical Direction Own firmware architecture, interface definitions, and hardware abstraction (HAL/API) standards across all product categories, globally. Establish architectural standards for real-time operating systems, connectivity frameworks, device intelligence, and edge processing. jobs.title: Director, Global Strategic Programs
jobs.description_text: About the Role The Director, Global Strategic Programs is a commercial leader responsible for converting SharkNinja's commercial ambition into measurable, repeatable outcomes — POS and revenue growth, margin, share, and the efficient investment of our global commercial spend. Operating as a trusted advisor to the Chief Commercial Officer and a key orchestrator of the commercial agenda, this leader aligns strategy, operating model, processes, and AI-enabled capabilities to accelerate value creation across the global commercial engine. The Director, Global Strategic Programs leads the execution of ACE (the Agentic Commercial Engine) and the broader portfolio of commercial initiatives — commercial intelligence, revenue growth management, category planning, media and social analytics, and international expansion. It requires exceptional commercial acumen, executive influence, and the ability to mobilize Sales, Marketing, Social, Finance, SS&A, and IT to deliver improvements in growth, margin, speed, and decision quality. The Director, Global Strategic Programs drives outcomes not only by solving problems, but by building the durable mechanisms, operating rhythms, and adoption that raise commercial performance across every category, market, and channel. What You'll Do: Commercial Strategy, Execution, and Growth Commercial Strategy & Alignment Translate the commercial growth agenda into clear programs, workstreams, KPIs, and execution plans tied to POS, revenue, margin, and share.

This role sets technical direction on the hardest connected-architecture problems in the portfolio and holds the technical standard that internal developers and external partners build against. The Principal Engineer designs the connected-platform interfaces and standards, then writes the reference implementations — connectivity stacks, provisioning and pairing code, display/UI frameworks, and app/cloud integration layers — that prove the architecture out in working code before any partner builds against it. That combination is what gives this role its leverage: not just interface contracts and design reviews, but hands-on implementation that sets the technical bar for the hardest connected-architecture problems in the portfolio. This is an architect-track role for an engineer who wants deep technical scope in connected systems without moving into people management. Key Responsibilities Technical Direction Define reference architectures and reference implementations for wireless connectivity, display/UI, and app/cloud integration reused across product categories. jobs.title: Program Manager - Quality Excellence
jobs.description_text: Position Overview: SharkNinja is building a new Product Excellence Program Management (PEPM) team — three roles, each owning a distinct phase of the product development lifecycle, working together to run one PE operating standard across the full lifecycle from inception to end-of-life. The vision is simple: four pods, one PE playbook — run faster. Consistent gates, escalation, and star reporting from Inception to EOL. Predicting star ratings before P0. Cutting in-market signal-to-fix to 10 days. Today, the handoffs across Product Excellence are not seamless enough. Quality insights generated upstream do not always reach the right downstream teams in time. In-market signals do not always make it back into NPD fast enough to influence the next generation. These three roles exist to close that loop — with speed. The ask for every PEPM is the same: Communicate. Act fast. Ensure the PE point of view is front and center. Each role is embedded at a specific phase of the development cycle, but all three operate as one team — sharing a common operating rhythm, a common PE playbook, and a shared accountability for ensuring nothing falls through the cracks between phases. All three roles report into VP, Product Excellence and Chief of Staff, and work in close partnership with each other, with the Product Excellence Functional leaders. jobs.title: Unit 26 - Software & System Architect Opportunities
jobs.description_text: Build the 26th We promise the world 25 new products a year. Unit 26 builds the 26th: SharkNinja itself. Inside a company moving as fast as ours, the highest-impact work doesn’t always fit neatly into anyone’s job description. It sits between functions and stays unsolved until someone owns it completely, builds the solution, proves its value, and ships it. That’s where Unit 26 comes in. Unit 26 is a small team of builders reporting to the Chief of Staff to the CEO, with executive sponsorship and access to the C-suite from day one. Our job is to solve problems that don’t have an obvious owner or an existing solution. When your build ships, you hand it to the business unit waiting on the other side and move to the next one. Zero to one, again and again. We’re starting with just eight builders, from inside SharkNinja and out. The Role You’ll work directly with teams across SharkNinja to understand what needs to change and what a successful solution must deliver. Then you own the build. What you make will flex with the problem: an app, an algorithm, an AI agent that eliminates thousands of hours of manual work, or a system that doesn’t yet exist at SharkNinja, or anywhere else. Some of your work will change how we run the company. Some will end up inside our products. Some will be things we haven’t imagined yet. Here, the building comes first. You’ll build on top of a global innovation engine that reaches tens of millions of homes, and you’ll have a stake in the value you create.

jobs.description_text: Our base salary range is $137,520 - $206,289, and in addition we have generous bonus plans to provide a competitive compensation package. Who We Are: We are a small product team at the Allen Institute for AI working on AI for the Planet. We're working on maritime conservation, food security, disaster resilience, and climate solutions with some of the most impactful organizations on the planet. Design, engineering, product, and partnerships work side by side with an ML research team, building products that support our environmental and high-impact users. Today, our team works on two products: Skylight provides AI-powered intelligence to combat illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing to protect our oceans. Governments, enforcement agencies, and conservation organizations in 95+ countries use Skylight data to protect their waters today via our interface, API, and most recently an agentic interface named Shippy. Read more at https://allenai.org/skylight . OlmoEarth is an open platform built around our family of foundation models for Earth observation. Users create custom fine-tuned models to detect and classify novel geospatial features. The platform handles the full loop: imagery acquisition, annotation, as well as model training and inference for ML and non-ML experts alike. Partners today include International Food Policy Research Institute, The Group on Earth Observation, NASA Harvest, Global Mangrove Watch, Amazon Conservation Alliance and more across for-good domains.
